title: 采集聚落
prompt:
Create a new art-direction concept for our miniature-planet civilization-management game using TWO reference images with clearly separate roles.

REFERENCE IMAGE 1 is the authority for the VISUAL STYLE: a warm, soft, semi-realistic stylized 3D miniature landscape, detailed organic vegetation, rounded weathered rocks, natural fine material variation, warm sandy ground, gentle sunlight and atmospheric miniature-diorama charm. Match its soft natural lighting, nuanced materials and pleasing proportions. The result must visibly adopt this reference's sophisticated natural appearance.

REFERENCE IMAGE 2 is the authority for the FUNCTIONAL PLANET LAYOUT AND DEVELOPMENT STAGE only. Preserve the full spherical world, camera angle, coastline, forest-resource location, rocky resource hill, central storage area and practical building relationships. Rebuild the geometry and materials into the style of image 1. Replace the prominent triangular flat-shaded land facets with softly rolling earth, subtle soil texture and patches of fine grass. Replace rigid triangular conifers with natural miniature woodland trees with individually suggested soft leaf clusters and readable trunks, still grouped into a resource forest. Use rounded weathered stone formations with subtle creases. Houses and factories become crafted miniature wood, stone and brick buildings with gently worn surfaces. Keep strong readable silhouettes and purposeful functional props. This is a visible style transformation, not a minor lighting change.

Landscape 1536 x 1024 composition. One COMPLETE miniature spherical planet, entire outline visible, a calm slightly elevated orbital management view. Preserve the globe scale and framing of image 2, with useful open margins. Buildings and trees stand upright relative to their LOCAL curved ground. The player manages the whole world; small residents and vehicles only illustrate automatic work. Gentle warm key light and neutral sky fill, soft shadows, restrained atmospheric glow, subtle focus falloff only outside the useful playable region. The world and working facilities must remain readable. Color palette: natural sage greens, muted golden crops, warm stone and wood, nuanced teal and blue ocean. Avoid harsh neon greens, obvious triangle mosaics, plastic toy surfaces or documentary photographic grit.

Keep a single calm coherent bay with stable simple coastline. Water is described by blue-green color layers, broad soft ripple highlights and understated light reflections. It has continuous curves and an elegant calm surface. Existing short agricultural channels are simple fixed ribbons with a few lengthwise motion streaks. No waterfall, no cascading river, no storm surf, no complicated foam simulation. Keep the water plausible as an attainable stylized game material.

Render SCENE ART ONLY: no UI, no writing, no labels, no numbers, no diagram arrows, no logo or watermark. We will add accurate game-management annotations separately. Do not import the leisure props from reference image 1: no beach chairs, umbrellas, decorative holiday tents or string lights. Every facility must belong to the resource, population, research or manufacturing economy specified for this stage. No spacecraft, no multiplayer battle, no second planet. Keep future development space visible.

STAGE-SPECIFIC GAMEPLAY BRIEF:
This is the first gathering settlement. Keep exactly the useful early economy visible in image 2: a timber logging lean-to at the forest edge with log piles; an open stone quarry at the rocky hill foot with squared stone and a simple tool rack; two modest thatched dwellings grouped at the existing residential location; a berry-gathering patch with baskets for food; and one larger open central stockpile with logs, stone and food sacks. Dirt paths connect these actual workplaces to storage. There are no cultivated fields, metal factories, vehicles or army yet. Small ambient workers illustrate job allocation. Keep the large open central-front/right grassland available for future farming and industry. The managerial choice is how to divide limited population between food, wood, stone and construction. Rebuild surfaces and foliage naturally, keeping the compact and sparse functional arrangement.
